inlines.v: DITCH, noun [G.] 1. A trench in the earth made by digging, particularly a trench for draining wet land, or for making a fence to guard inclosures, or for preventing an enemy from approaching a town or fortress. In the latter sense, it is called also a foss or moat, and is dug round the rampart or wall between the scarp and counterscarp. 2. Any long, hollow receptacle of water. DITCH, verb intransitive To dig or make a ditch or ditches. DITCH, verb transitive 1. To dig a ditch or ditches in; to drain by a ditch; as, to ditch moist land. 2. To surround with a ditch
